common.schematic: Rows follow a filling guide, not measured energy spacings. Arrows label spin projections.
common.rules: Pauli: at most two opposite arrows per orbital. Hund: occupy equal-energy orbitals separately with parallel arrows before pairing. Aufbau is a filling guide with observed exceptions.
common.transition: For d-block chemistry, the d electrons can also participate in bonding.
common.exception: Observed reference differs from the simple filling rule (Cr, Cu). Electron interactions matter; the diagram is not an energy calculation.
common.ionRule: The nucleus stays fixed. Cations lose electrons; anions gain electrons. For these transition-metal cations, remove ns electrons before (n−1)d electrons.
common.ionScope: Common-ion configuration model; it does not predict whether an isolated ion is stable.
common.help: Click an orbital to cycle it: empty → ↑ → ↑↓ → empty. Drag ↑ or ↓ from the tray onto an orbital, drag an arrow to another orbital, or drag it off the diagram to remove it. Keyboard: Space cycles, U adds ↑, D adds ↓, Delete removes.

mobile.help: Use the scroll bar, wheel, or swipe outside controls. Keyboard focus brings controls into view.

common.shellCaption: Electrons grouped by shell n. A counting view, not orbits.

messages.ready: Explore the diagram or check your prediction.
messages.pauli: Pauli: that spin projection is already occupied in this orbital. The opposite spin may share it.
messages.count: The target needs {{target}} electrons; the diagram has {{count}}.
messages.higher: The electron count is right. This allowed occupancy does not match the ground-state reference. Check which subshells are occupied.
messages.hund: The subshell counts are right. For ground-state filling, spread parallel arrows among equal-energy orbitals before pairing.
messages.ground: Matches ground-state filling. Equivalent orbital choices and reversed spin arrows are accepted.
messages.again: Try again. Compare the electron counts or the filling rules.
messages.explore: Choose an element to compare its reference configuration with the filling-rule prediction.
messages.ionReady: Gain or lose electrons one at a time until the diagram shows the target ion.
messages.limit: That step would go past the target ion or the neutral atom. Try the other button.
messages.anomaly: Last electron placed. The observed ground state rearranges the 4s and 3d electrons relative to the simple filling rule.

prompts.repair: Repair the diagram so it matches ground-state filling.
prompts.identify: Which neutral element has this configuration?
prompts.isoelectronic: Which neutral atom has the same number of electrons as this ion?
prompts.classify: Does this diagram match ground-state filling?
prompts.move: One electron is in the wrong orbital. Drag it to where it belongs, then Check.

a11y.controls: Choose an element or ion, select orbital boxes, and use the named action buttons. Reset restores this screen.
